messages:
Alice Chen: Heads-up — after the CUDA 13 probe landed on h100s I see a p99 latency spike for short sequences. seq<=9 p99 went from ~22ms -> ~48ms on prod traffic. Autotune logs show a kernel pick flip at seq=9. Any quick ideas?

Raj Patel: Can you paste the autotune pick lines + model/quantization? Is this q4/q8 model?

Alice Chen: Model: rwin-13b-q4f. Quant: q4f-std. Autotune snippet below (copied from runtime telemetry):
```
[autotune] seq=8  -> kernel=vec_attn_v3    score=87.2  path=vectorized
[autotune] seq=9  -> kernel=scalar_attn_v1 score=98.9  path=scalar_fallback  (tie_breaker_delta=11.7)
[autotune] kvcache_enabled=true  prefix_len=2
```
Also saw the change only when KV cache is warm; cold-start latencies unaffected.

Mei Wong: We repro'ed something similar on staging last night for llama-2-13b-q4: once prefix_len>0, the batch/KV stride heuristic pushes us off the vec path. Driver warp scheduling in 13.x can change occupancy behavior, so autotuner's score model might shift.

Tom Becker: Quick checks: is KERNEL_PREFETCH_THRESHOLD still 8 on those pods? If the driver changed warp occupancy, the threshold math could mis-evaluate and prefer scalar kernels. Run: `kubectl exec -c runtime <pod> -- printenv | grep KERNEL_PREFETCH_THRESHOLD`

Alice Chen: Confirmed env=8 on canary pool. Ran microbench with bench-bot:
```
bench-bot: microbench --model rwin-13b-q4f --seq 8 --batch 1 --kv-warm -> p99=23ms
bench-bot: microbench --model rwin-13b-q4f --seq 9 --batch 1 --kv-warm -> p99=49ms
```
Repro is very stable locally on our h100 canary VM.

Raj Patel: Since it's deterministic, two levers: temporary runtime tie-breaker favoring vectorized kernel for seq <= 12 when delta < X%, or revert the driver on affected hosts. Ops usually prefers runtime controls.

Mei Wong: I can push a runtime-config override to prefer `vec_attn_v3` up to seq 12 for 10% traffic in us-west-2. Also enable full autotune trace logging for those pods so we get richer telemetry.

Alice Chen: That sounds good. I'll prepare a small patch to the kernel selector: change tie-breaker to prefer the vectorized path if (delta_score < 15) AND (kvcache_enabled == true) AND (seq <= 12). Add a unit + smoke test asserting p99 < 30ms for seq<=9.

Tom Becker: Ops note — if you need to roll back quickly, we can also pin the runtime to the previous kernel-ranking table via `runtime-config.kernels.rank: v2024-11-21` until the canary proves stable.

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: rollout_id=rl-2024-11-17-88, scope=us-west-2/h100-canary-02, traffic=10%. Kernel-pick traces enabled.

Mei Wong: I'll watch the telemetry dashboard and attach the autotune traces to the ticket. If p99 still >35ms after 2 hours we roll forward the driver rollback plan.

Alice Chen: Opening the PR + ticket now. PR will include the selector tweak, smoke test, and a runtime-config snippet for ops. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

bench-bot: Synthetic regression test added to CI: `ci/perf/shortseq-kernel-flip` — will run on every runtime change.

Raj Patel: Perfect. Keep an eye on end-to-end evals (generation quality) — changing kernel ordering can subtly affect numerics for quantized paths.

Alice Chen: Noted — I'll include eval run on the same commit. Will update the thread with the ticket/PR numbers shortly.
